subject: Request: temporary latency tolerance & staged rollback plan for model12-gamma
messages:
From: Samira Patel <samira@finflux.com>

Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Model12-gamma p95 latency increase - impact to live flows

Hi Tessa,

Over the last 2 hours we've been seeing our checkout service p95 jump from ~220ms to ~980ms for calls backed by model12-gamma. This began just after 07:00 UTC and coincides with a deployment window on your side per our webhook logs. Impact: some customers are experiencing timeouts and we had two payment failures that retried.

We've attached a short trace and our SRE logs (repro-logs-20280529.zip). Can you confirm if you rolled model12 to a new variant or changed routing? This is blocking our Friday releases.

Thanks,
Samira Patel
Senior Platform Engineer, FinFlux Payments

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>

Marcus / Neha — forwarding an urgent customer impact from FinFlux. They report a ~1s p95 on model12-gamma since ~07:00 UTC; their logs point to a version rollout on our side. Can the serving/runtime team triage whether any recent kernel/kernel-selection or quantization promotions hit model12-gamma in that window?

Customer asked for next steps and whether we can revert to the prior variant if needed. I recommend we prepare a staged rollback runbook (quick fallback -> canary -> full) and request a temporary SLA tolerance while we execute.

Please acknowledge and share estimated time to a rollback decision. I will loop in customer once we have a plan.

Tessa Morgan

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Model12-gamma p95 latency increase - impact to live flows

On Tue, May 29, 2028 at 09:31 AM Tessa Morgan wrote:
> Marcus / Neha — forwarding an urgent customer impact from FinFlux.

Acknowledged. Initial checks: there was a promotion of model12-gamma v12.3.1 -> v12.3.2 at 06:58 UTC (automated rollout for perf regressions eliminated in canary but this one got wider due to traffic shift). Kernel-selection logs show a new attention kernel landed for this variant that increases throughput but appears to regress tail latency on longer contexts.

What I need now to make a safe call:
- 1) p50/p95/p99 trend for the last 4 hours (please see attached p95-trends-model12_gamma-20280529.png).
- 2) a grace window approval from sales/ops to perform a staged rollback (we should start with a 10% traffic fallback to v12.3.1 for 30 minutes and observe).
- 3) runbook approval for rollforward if rollback fails.

I can assemble the rollback steps and automation hooks in 30–45m once I have approval to act. If we do not get approval, our suggested mitigation is to temporarily increase request timeouts on FinFlux side and enable prefix caching for common flows.

Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachments: p95-trends-model12_gamma-20280529.png
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira@finflux.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 10:50:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Model12-gamma p95 latency increase - proposed plan and ask for SLA tolerance

Samira — thanks for the quick signal and the logs. We believe the increase aligns with an internal promotion of model12-gamma variant v12.3.2. Marcus proposes a staged rollback (10% -> 50% -> 100%) to the previous variant v12.3.1 with monitoring at each step. Estimated wall-clock for a full rollback if the canary looks good: ~90 minutes.

Ask: can you accept a short SLA tolerance window (p95 may remain elevated during the 30m canary) and temporarily increase client-side timeout to 2.5s during the switchover? We will not perform a full rollback without your go-ahead.

I am also requesting internal temporary SLA carveout authorization so we can proceed without causing support alerts for the customer.

Proposed schedule:
- 11:30 UTC: run 10% fallback (30m monitor)
- 12:05 UTC: expand to 50% (30m monitor)
- 12:45 UTC: full rollback if metrics stable

I'll attach the short runbook and metrics link.

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: staged-rollback-runbook-v1.md; https://drive.redwood.com/finflux/model12_gamma/metrics-20280529
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 11:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: temporary latency tolerance & staged rollback plan for model12-gamma

Tessa / team — I reviewed Marcus' notes and the attached p95 trends. Given the customer impact and the clear correlation with the v12.3.2 promotion, I authorize a temporary SLA tolerance and green-light the staged rollback plan as described. Conditions:
- Limit the initial canary to 10% and hold for 30m with automated metric-based aborts (p95 improvement >= 200ms or error rate increase > 0.2%).
- Notify FinFlux SRE before each expansion step.
- Capture a post-mortem and proposed mitigation (kernel rollback + regression test) within 72 hours.

Neha, please ensure billing/credit teams are prepped in case FinFlux asks for a short service credit; we should be ready to propose a one-off operational credit if the rollback does not fully remediate.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
